testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to show that the system is broken.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are yellow. Even if the ABS is not working, your regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: If your brakes are hot after driving down a steep hill, let them cool before using the parking brake. Using the parking brake when brakes are hot can damage them.

questions.question: A load that is 40 feet long should be secured with at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The number of alcoholic drinks consumed
How fast the alcoholic drinks were consumed

questions.explanation: BAC is determined by three things: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the person's weight.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These remove water and oil that build up inside. They can be operated by hand or automatically.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, you must:
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you need to leave the engine running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.
Use only braking to slow down.

questions.explanation: On steep downhills, use the engine to slow your speed. Shift to a lower gear before starting down. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until construction is done to drive.

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: The highest air pressure for a tire
The most weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure
The least weight a tire can carry
The average weight of a vehicle's tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The most weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure
questions.explanation: Tire load is the most weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. This number is printed on the tire's side.

questions.question: Spring brakes turn on when:

options.text: Too much air pressure is lost.
A dashboard control is turned on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops too low. When you see the low pressure warning, safely leave the road and stop while you still have brake control.

questions.question: When can you properly check mirror adjustment?

options.text: When there is no trailer attached to the tractor.
When the vehicle is on a slight incline.
When the vehicle is on a slight decline.

questions.explanation: You can only check mirror adjustment accurately when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Why should you cover cargo?

options.text: To protect the cargo from thieves.
To protect the cargo from weather.
To prevent other drivers from seeing what you are transporting.
To keep the cargo a secret.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from weather.
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect it from weather and to keep it from spilling onto other drivers.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure releases to slow the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver?
questions.explanation: Give a distracted driver plenty of space. Be careful when passing because the driver may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper if possible when driving in reverse.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the truck and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Walk around the vehicle first to check for hazards. Use both mirrors while backing and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: How does friction occur in an S-cam brake?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the outside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What is a good rule when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get the attention of other drivers.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal early so drivers behind you know your plans. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To prevent cargo from being loaded too high.
To prevent cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, or on the sides of cargo to keep it from sliding when the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What should you not do at a railroad crossing during a driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle if it is moving too slowly on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad crossing.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on specific driving moves and general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and signals, and avoid accidents or violations.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should not roll backwards when starting from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: Which of the following may result in being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Being considered a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.correctAnswerText: Being considered a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if the TSA considers you a security threat. Other reasons include renouncing U.S. citizenship, not being a lawful permanent resident, or being convicted of certain crimes.

questions.question: If there are no warning gates or lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are likely abandoned.
Park your vehicle and walk up to the tracks to check for trains.
Look down the tracks in both directions to see if a train is coming.
Do whatever surrounding vehicles are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look down the tracks in both directions to see if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look both directions down the tracks to check for approaching trains.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: Multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions are used:

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly.
To make a vehicle less noisy.

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions provide extra gears. They are controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before starting a trip:

options.text: They will likely become clean after driving a short distance.
It should not be a concern.
They should be cleaned before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be cleaned before driving.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt or anything that could block your view. Clean them as needed.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Can only be done in dry weather.

questions.explanation: Cargo should be blocked to prevent it from moving around during transport. Shifting cargo can make steering and handling difficult.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal could damage the brakes by putting too much pressure on them.

questions.question: When driving long distances, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving. Driving when you are normally asleep increases the risk of falling asleep at the wheel.

questions.question: What is the legal maximum width for a vehicle and its load?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin law allows vehicles (including their load) to be no wider than 8 feet 6 inches.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual brake system, when should you start driving?

options.text: After the vehicle warms up so fuel reaches the engine.
After the air compressor builds 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
After pumping the pedal about 20 times to build pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the air compressor builds 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before you start driving.

questions.question: What is required when transporting hanging meat in a refrigerated truck?

options.text: It is good experience for new drivers.
It is illegal in most states.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat creates an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity and the meat swings as the truck moves. This affects how you can control the vehicle. You need skill to drive safely with this type of cargo.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, how quickly do air brakes work?

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: Why should flares be used with caution after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see flares when it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Fires often start after accidents when flares are used near spilled fuel. Always use flares with caution.

questions.question: What do drivers often do when stuck behind a slow-moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, when does the truck get affected?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is near the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay of a few seconds between when you hear a tire fail and when you feel it affect the truck. The delay is short enough that you might think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks have drains to remove water and oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, it is good on long trips.

questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous. It takes your attention off the road and requires you to take one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: How can you best avoid hitting a hazard on the road?

options.text: Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving away from a hazard is safer than trying to stop. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: Which sign does NOT mean the brakes are damaged?

options.text: Oil or grease on the shoes
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: Signs of brake damage include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and worn or broken shoes. Pads that are clean and free of oil or grease are in good condition.

questions.question: What should you know about joggers wearing headsets?

options.text: They are usually aware of their surroundings.
They may not notice what is happening around them.
They can clearly hear traffic sounds.
They usually have no music playing.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not notice what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Watch out for joggers, pedestrians, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic sounds and may not know you are there.

questions.question: What can happen if cargo is loaded badly?

options.text: It looks bad to others on the road.
It can injure the driver during a quick stop.
It makes it easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can injure the driver during a quick stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded and secured properly. During a quick stop, badly loaded cargo could shift or fall and hurt or kill the driver.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In air brake vehicles, a knob controls the parking brake. Pull the knob to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead. This gives you more room to avoid sudden stops and gives the tailgater room to pass. Do not speed up, as this can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: On an uphill grade, what does gravity do to your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle down when you go uphill. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require what to change gears?
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need double clutching to shift gears. This technique takes practice to master.
